headline: Simulating coupled genetic and antigenic or resistance evolution in influenza and HIV-1
label: Pathogen Evolution Simulation And Forecasting
summary: Forward-time and inference models now link sequence variation to antigenic, resistance, and conformational phenotypes in influenza and HIV-1 protease.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit coupling of sequence variation to a phenotype within simulation or inference. antigen-prime is a forward-time epidemic simulator that links genetic sequence to antigenic phenotype under host immune selection and is used to benchmark influenza variant assignment. A published HIV-1 protease study forecasts drug-resistant protease evolution under protease inhibitor treatment. A second HIV-1 protease study couples AlphaFold2 ensembles at varying MSA depths to a coarse-grained Langevin model to estimate conformational time scales, tested on protease variants. This study addresses dynamics rather than evolution, so it is adjacent to the others. What is new is the explicit linkage of sequence to antigenic, resistance-related, or conformational phenotype within simulation or inference, rather than direct observation of these relationships.
